## Public Types

- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.AccessibilityOptionsRegistry (class, common): Central registry for accessibility option widgets that PolyLib injects into the vanilla Accessibility Options screen.

Mods register providers during client init. PolyLib's event handlers call `#inject(Screen)` on every screen init event. Usage example `// During client init: AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register("mymod.rescue", target -> { target.addCategory(Component.literal("My Mod")); target.addToggle(Component.literal("Fall Rescue"), prefs::isRescueOn, prefs::setRescueOn); `); }
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.AccessibilityPolicy (enum, common): Controls how a registered accessibility preference interacts with server configuration.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.AccessibilityPrefsC2SPayload (record, common): C2S packet: client sends its current accessibility preference values to the server. Only preferences with effective policy `AccessibilityPolicy#PLAYER_OVERRIDES_SERVER` are included.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.AccessibilityPrefsManager (class, common): Server-side store for per-player accessibility preferences.

Pure common — no loader API. Thread-safe via `ConcurrentHashMap`. Values are stored exactly as received from the client; no server config gate is applied here. The policy check (`AccessibilityPolicy`) is enforced on the client before sending.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.AccessibilityRegistrationBuilder (class, common): Fluent builder for registering accessibility options while simultaneously contributing their default English translations to PolyLib's lang datagen system.

Used with the builder-style `AccessibilityOptionsRegistry#register` overloads: `AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register("mymod.rescue", builder -> builder .togglePair( "mymod.accessibility.rescue_blink", "Save Me: Blink", () -> prefs.blinkRescueOn, v -> prefs.blinkRescueOn = v, "mymod.accessibility.rescue_farreach", "Save Me: Far Reach", () -> prefs.farReachOn, v -> prefs.farReachOn = v ) .toggle( "mymod.accessibility.void_grave", "Void Grave", () -> prefs.voidGraveOn, v -> prefs.voidGraveOn = v ) ); `

Each method contributes the given key+English pair to `PolyLangContributions` and stores the corresponding widget action. The builder itself implements `OptionsWidgetProvider` and is stored as the entry's provider.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.OptionsListTarget (class, common): Wraps a reflected `OptionsList` and exposes a concise builder API for adding widgets to the Accessibility Options screen.

Uses reflection to call the NeoForge-patched `addSmall(AbstractWidget, AbstractWidget)` and `addBig(AbstractWidget)` overloads which are not present in the vanilla compile target.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.accessibility.OptionsWidgetProvider (interface, common): Callback that adds one or more widgets to the Accessibility Options screen via `OptionsListTarget`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.BlockFacing (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.ChangeListener (interface, common): Can be implemented by any `BlockEntity` whose block extends `PolyEntityBlock`. Allows the block entity to receive neighbor change events from the block.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.DataRetainingBlock (interface, common): This class can be implemented on any `BlockEntity`, then as long as that entity belongs to a `PolyEntityBlock`, It will keep its data when harvested.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.InteractableBlock (interface, common): Can be implemented by any `BlockEntity` whose block extends `PolyEntityBlock`. Allows the block entity to receive player interaction events.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.PolyBlock (class, common): Base block class for PolyLib,
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.PolyBlockEntity (class, common): Base class for all poly block entities. This implements the data manager system as well as a bunch of other useful features. Designed to work with `PolyBlockEntity`
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.PolyEntityBlock (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.RedstoneActivatedBlock (interface, common): All functionality for this interface is already built into `PolyBlockEntity` This means all you have to do is implement this on a `BlockEntity` that extends PolyBlockEntity. you can then use `PolyBlockEntity#isTileEnabled()` to check if the tile is currently allowed to run.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.blocks.RedstoneEmitter (interface, common): Can be implemented by any `BlockEntity` whose block extends `PolyEntityBlock`. Note: canProvidePower must be set to true on the `PolyEntityBlock` constructor.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.ChatChannel (class, common): Represents an isolated stream of messages and members.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.ChatConfig (class, common): User-facing config options for the PolyLib chat system. Values are runtime defaults; these can be wired to a config screen in the future.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.ChatMember (record, common): Represents a member/participant in a ChatChannel sidebar. Can represent a Player, a Shell, or an Automation Controller.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.ChatRouter (class, common): Manages active chat channels and routes messages.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.ChatNotifications (class, common): Registry for mention/notification triggers per channel. When a message arrives on a channel, the registered trigger is tested. If it fires, the channel's UI elements pulse and an optional vanilla notification is sent.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.ChatWindowManager (class, common): Manages multiple GuiWindows, handles Z-indexing, focus, snapping, and tiling.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.FloatingChatWindow (class, common): The actual chat UI that renders a ChatChannel.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.FloatingNotificationWindow (class, common): Floating notification window — read-only scrollable list of NotificationEntry items. ALERT entries pulse the header yellow→orange. Inherits drag/minimize/resize from GuiWindow.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.NotificationEntry (record, common): A single notification pushed by a mod.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.NotificationSeverity (enum, common): Severity level for a notification entry. ALERT entries trigger window border pulse.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.NotificationWindowManager (class, common): Manages FloatingNotificationWindow instances for FLOATING-mode notification windows.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.NotificationWindowMode (enum, common): How a notification window is displayed.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.NotificationWindowRegistry (class, common): Registry for notification windows. Mods register named windows and push entries to them.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.notification.PolyNotifications (class, common): Convenience API for the built-in shared PolyLib notification window. All mods sending to `#send(NotificationEntry)` share one consolidated panel.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.PulseEffect (class, common): Generates a pulsing ARGB color that cycles between two colors over time. Used for mention pulse on floating window headers and tab badges.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.AllTab (record, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChannelTab (record, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTab (interface, common): Sealed interface for tab types shown in the vanilla chat tab bar.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTabBarElement (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTabBarSide (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTabBarTop (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTabInjection (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.ChatTabRegistry (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.NotificationTab (record, common): A tab representing a notification window within the chat tab bar.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.TabPosition (enum, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.tab.VanillaTab (record, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.client.VanillaChatResize (class, common): Opt-in API for making the vanilla chat area resizable. PolyLib does NOT register this by default. Mods call `#enable()` to opt in. When enabled, the vanilla chat history region gains drag handles on its top and right edges, allowing the player to resize the chat area. The resized dimensions are persisted in ChatLayoutManager under a special layout ID.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.layout.ChatLayoutManager (class, common): Manages saving and loading of ChatWindowLayouts to the local client disk.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.layout.ChatWindowLayout (class, common): Represents the on-screen layout properties of a floating chat window. This state is persisted to disk.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.layout.SnapCorner (enum, common): Screen corner a floating window is snapped to. When snapped, the window re-anchors on screen resize.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.chat.RichChatMessage (record, common): Represents a single message in the PolyLib Modular Chat Framework.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.config.ConfigPanelRegistry (class, common): Central registry for mod config panel screens. Registration tiers

Vanilla Screen — `ScreenFactory)`. Works on any loader. The dev provides a standard `Screen` factory. ModularGui — `GuiProviderFactory)`. PolyLib wraps the `GuiProvider` in a `ModularGuiScreen` automatically. ModularGui Injection — `Predicate, Function)`. Overlays a ModularGui directly onto an existing vanilla screen via `ModularGuiInjector`. Use for advanced cases only.

Auto-hooks

NeoForge — use `NeoForgeConfigHelper.register(...)` from the NeoForge module. This calls both this registry AND `IConfigScreenFactory` so the entry appears under the native "Mods → Config" button. Fabric / Mod Menu — handled automatically via PolyLib's `ModMenuCompat` entrypoint when Mod Menu is present. Just call `#register` from the Fabric init. Button injection fallback — PolyLib injects a button into `ConfigurationSectionScreen` and similar screens that the native hook doesn't cover. Keybinds are also ticked via `#tickKeybinds()`.

PolyConfig json5 backing The per-mod keybind enable/disable map is stored in `polylib.json5` and managed through `PolylibCommon#configData`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.config.GuiProviderFactory (interface, common): Factory that creates a PolyLib `GuiProvider` for a given parent screen. PolyLib wraps this in `net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.ModularGuiScreen` automatically.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.config.KeyboardShortcut (record, common): Describes an optional keyboard shortcut for a config panel entry. Variants

`#unbound(KeyMapping.Category)` — shows in Controls but has no default key `InputConstants.Type, KeyMapping.Category)` — has a suggested key but defaults to UNBOUND so it never conflicts `InputConstants.Type, KeyMapping.Category)` — bound by default; use sparingly

Create or reuse a `KeyMapping.Category` via `KeyMapping.Category.register(Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath(modId, "main"))`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.config.ScreenFactory (interface, common): Factory that creates a config `Screen` for a given parent screen. Used by `ConfigPanelRegistry` to open a mod's config panel.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.gif.AnimatedGif (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.gif.GifSequenceWriter (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.gif.ImageUtils (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.model.Model3D (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiButton (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiColourPicker (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiContextMenu (class, common): Context menus get added to the root element when they are created so as long as no new elements are added after the menu is opened, the menu will always be on top. It will also automatically close when an option is selected, or when the user clicks outside the context menu.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiDialog (class, common): This class provides an easy way to construct a simple dialog with some text and buttons.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiDropZone (class, common): A translucent highlight rectangle shown as a drop-zone indicator during drag operations. Starts hidden; call `#show()` / `#hide()` to toggle visibility.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiDVD (class, common): Just for fun!
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiElement (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiEnergyBar (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiEntityRenderer (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiFuzzyFinder (class, common): A search-based context menu overlay (Fuzzy Finder) for visual scripting. Allows users to type to filter a list of available nodes or options.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiFuzzySearch (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiInfoPanel (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiItemStack (class, common): A simple gui element that renders an item stack. This width and height of this element should be constrained to the same value, The stack size is based on the element size. constrain size to 16x16 for the standard gui stack size.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiList (class, common): GuiList, as the name suggests allows you to display a list of objects. The list type can be whatever you want, and you can install a converter to map list objects to elements for display.

The default converter simply displays the toString() value of the object.

Element width will be fixed to the width of the GuiList, element height can be whatever you want.

Note on adding child elements to this: If any child elements extend beyond the bounds of this element, that part will be culled. Also, child elements will always end up bellow the list items when the list is updated.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiManipulable (class, common): This element can be used to create movable/resizable guis of gui elements. This is achieved via a "contentElement" to which all child elements should eb attached. Initially the bounds of the content element will match the parent `GuiManipulable` element. However, depending on which features are enabled, it is possible for the user to resize the content element by clicking and dragging the edges, or move the element by clicking and dragging a specified "dragArea".

It should be noted that the constraints on the underlying `GuiManipulable` should be fairly rigid. Things like dynamic constraint changes will not translate through to the contentElement,

If a UI resize occurs the content element's bounds will be reset to default. You can also trigger a manual reset by calling `#resetBounds()`
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiPannableCanvas (class, common): A generic panning/zooming canvas element. Provides: - panX, panY, zoom state - Coordinate transformations between Screen Space and Canvas Space - Middle-mouse dragging to pan - Scroll wheel to zoom toward cursor - Bookmark saving/recalling for viewport positions
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiProgressIcon (class, common): This can be used to create a simple progress indicator like those used in machines like furnaces.

The background texture (if one is used) and the animated texture must be the same shape and size, They must be designed so that the animated texture can be rendered directly on top of the background texture with no offset. The animated texture should not have any empty space on ether end as the entire width of the texture is used in the animation.

Texture must be designed for left to right animation,
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiRectangle (class, common): Used to draw a simple rectangle on the screen. Can specify separate (or no) border colours and fill colours. Can also render using the "shadedRectangle" render type.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiScrolling (class, common): So the logic behind this element is as follows. This element contains a base "Content Element" that holds all the scrollable content. The content element's position is controlled by the `GuiScrolling` But its `GeoParam#WIDTH` and `GeoParam#HEIGHT` constraints can be set by the user, Or they can be set to dynamically adjust to the child elements added to it.

The bounds of the `GuiScrolling` represent the "view window" When scrolling up/down, left/right the Content Element is effectively just moving around behind the view window and everything outside the view window is scissored off. Any events that occur outside the view window are not propagated to scroll element. Calls to `#isMouseOver()` from an area of an element that is outside the view window will return false.

Elements that are completely outside the view window will not be rendered at all for efficiency.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiSlider (class, common): This can be used as the base for anything that requires the linear movement of an element between two position. e.g. Scroll bars, Slide controls and slide indicators.

Implementation is simple, Simply install a "Slide Element", this will be the moving element, The movement of this element is confined to the bounds og the `GuiSlider`

The position of the slider is managed via the installed `SliderState`
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiSlots (class, common): This element is used to manage and render a grid of inventory slots in a GUI. The width and height of this element are automatically constrained based on the slot configuration. However, you can override those constraints, The slot grid will always render in the center of the element nomater the element size.

This can be used to render all slots in a `SlotGroup` or a sub-set of slots within a group.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiText (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiTextField (class, common): TODO, Re write this, Its currently mostly pulled from the TextField in Gui v2
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiTextList (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiTexture (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.GuiWindow (class, common): A draggable, floating window primitive built on GuiManipulable. Supports window titles, close buttons, and tab-group docking logic.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.elements.TextInputDialog (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.Assembly (class, common): This represents multiple gui elements that have been assembled into a functional component. This is primarily for used by the built-in element builders. But could be used in custom builders.

This is needed because a builder method for an element, cant always return just the relevant element. Take the scroll bar for example. The builtin scroll bar construction consists of a background element, with the scroll bar itself being a child of the background element constrained to the background element.

So the create method for a scroll bar needs to return the background element so that you can constrain int appropriately, but it also needs to return the slider element so that you can actually use it. That's what this container class is for.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.BackgroundRender (interface, common): Allows a Gui Elements to render content behind child elements. This is the default render mode for the majority of elements.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.ColourState (interface, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.Constraints (class, common): This class contains a bunch of static helper methods that can be used to quickly apply common constraints. The plan is to keep adding common constraints to this class as they pop up.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.container.ContainerGuiProvider (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.container.ContainerScreenAccess (interface, common): Used by `ContainerGuiProvider` Provides access to the ContainerMenu as well as some essential functions.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.container.DataSync (class, common): This class provides a convenient way to synchronize server side data with a client side screen via the ContainerMenu
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.container.SlotGroup (class, common): Used to configure slots a set of slots in a ContainerMenu. The SlotGroup can then be passed to ModularGui elements such as `GuiSlots` in order to give the gui control over slot positioning and rendering.

Ideally you should use a separate SlotGroup for each 'group' of slots, Meaning the players main inventory and hot bar should be separate ranges. That said, if you have multiple slots spread out across something like a machine gui, You can add them all to one SlotGroup then pass each individual slot from that range to a `ContainerScreenAccess, SlotGroup, int)`
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.ContentElement (interface, common): Implemented by elements that have a separate child element to which content should be added. e.g. scroll element, manipulable element etc...

- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.ElementEvents (interface, common): This class defines the default implementation for all Screen events. Input events in Modular GUI v2 work similar to v2, events are passed to all elements recursively in a top-down order, and if any element 'consumes' the event, it will not be passed any further down the chain. However, this approach had issues in v2, because there are certain situations where an element needs to receive an event even if it has been consumed. To deal with that we now have two methods for each event, the main handler method that will always get called, and uses a 'consumed' flag to track whether the event has been consumed, as well as a simpler convenience method that will only get called if the event has not already been canceled, and does not require you to call super.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.ForegroundRender (interface, common): Allows a Gui Elements to render content in front of child elements. Note: Most elements should use `BackgroundRender` to render their content.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.Align (enum, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.Axis (enum, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.AxisConfig (enum, common): Denies how each of the three axis parameters are computed based on the available constraints. Note: If both min and max are defined, size is ignored.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.Borders (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.ConstrainedGeometry (class, common): This is the base class used to define the size and position of a GuiElement.

The geometry system is designed to be very user-friendly, yet very powerful, with the ability to do all sorts of fun and interesting things. But if all you want is the ability to set simple size and position values, then there is no need to read any further. Just use the basic setters setXPos, setYPos, setWidth, setHeight and everything should just work. If you want to dive deeper, read on.

The geometry system is based around 6 core parameters: xMin, xMax, xSize, yMin, yMax and ySize. See: `GeoParam`

These parameters are defined using 'Constraints' See: `Constraint`

When properly constrained, it will be possible to request values for any of these 6 parameters.

For each axis (x and y) there are 3 constraints: min, max and size.

In order for an axis to be properly defined 2 of these constraints need to be set.

e.g. (xMin and xSize) or (xMin and xMax) or (xMax and xSize)

Using any of these combinations the position and size of an axis can be computed.

Look at `AxisConfig` for details on the values that get returned when too few constraints are set.

TLDR: We will always try to return "reasonable" default values. e.g. if only size is constrained, xMin will default to 0 and xMax will default to 0 + xSize.

If all three constraints are set then the size constraint will be ignored.

You can use `#strictMode(boolean)` to change this behavior.

There are a number of different types of constraints that can be used, including completely custom constraints.

Take a look at the `Constraint` class for a detailed list with explanations.

Note: All position and size values in ModularGui use doubles. This is because floating point position and size values can be very useful at times. But they can also cause a lot of ugly visual artifacts when not used properly. So by default, all the builtin constraints will cast their outputs to an integer value. If you need floating point precision, you can enable it by calling .precise() on any of the builtin constraints.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.Constraint (interface, common): Constraints are used to define an elements position and shape by constraining the elements geometry parameters. `GeoParam` Constraints can be as simple as literal values representing an elements exact position and / or size in screen space, They can be relative coordinates, (Relative to another element's Geometry) Or they can be used to supply completely custom dynamic values.

All the built-in constraints are implemented and documented in this class.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.ConstraintImpl (class, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.Direction (enum, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.GeoParam (enum, common): Used to define the 6 core parameters that make up an elements geometry These are named Left, Right, Width, Top, Bottom, Height. These names were chosen for ease of use, and to make it clear what they represent. Internally they are known as xMin, xMax, xSize, yMin, yMax, ySize.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.client.modulargui.lib.geometry.GeoRef (class, common): Used to access one of the 6 core parameters that make up an element's geometry.

The primary purpose of this class is to provide a convenient way to reference a geometry parameter when defining constraints. It also helps make the code more debuggable. I could just make literally everything a lambda, but that makes debugging kinda painful when things break.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.data.lang.PolyLangContributions (class, common): Central store for PolyLib-managed default English translation strings.

Populated automatically by PolyLib registration APIs:

`AccessibilityRegistrationBuilder` toggle/pair/category methods `ConfigPanelRegistry.register(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, ...)` overloads `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry.register(..., displayKey, displayEnglish)` overload `PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier)` overload Direct: `String)`

Consumed by `PolyLibLangProvider` in PolyLib's NeoForge module during datagen. Mod lang providers should extend `PolyLibLangProvider` instead of `LanguageProvider` directly to receive all contributions automatically.

Thread-safe. First registration wins — later contributions for an existing key are ignored, allowing mods to override PolyLib defaults by contributing earlier.

Created for DisCraftHonored PolyLib integration.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.data.TileDataManager (class, common): This class provides a way to save and synchronize tile data with the client. As well as the ability to set fields in your tile via a client side container screen.

To get started simply define a TileDataManager instance in your tile and call the `#tick()`, and methods from the appropriate methods on your tile.

You can then define a data field in you tile like so: public IntData myIntField = dataManager.register("int_field_name", new IntData(0), SAVE, SYNC, CLIENT_CONTROL);

The SAVE, SYNC and CLIENT_CONTROL flags are each optional, Take a look at #register(String, AbstractDataStore, int...) for more info.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.datagen.FabricPolyLibLangProvider (class, fabric): Abstract `FabricLanguageProvider` that automatically includes every translation entry contributed to PolyLib's lang datagen system via any PolyLib registration API. Usage Extend this class in your mod's Fabric datagen module instead of extending `FabricLanguageProvider` directly: `public class ModLangProvider extends FabricPolyLibLangProvider { public ModLangProvider(FabricPackOutput output, CompletableFuture registries) { super(output, registries); ` protected void addModTranslations(HolderLookup.Provider registries, TranslationBuilder builder) { // Only entries NOT managed by PolyLib registration APIs. } } }
- net.creeperhost.polylib.datagen.PolyLibLangProvider (class, neoforge): Abstract `LanguageProvider` that automatically includes every translation entry contributed to PolyLib's lang datagen system via any PolyLib registration API. Usage Extend this class in your mod's NeoForge datagen module instead of extending `LanguageProvider` directly: `public class ModLangProvider extends PolyLibLangProvider { public ModLangProvider(PackOutput output) { super(output, "mymod"); ` protected void addModTranslations() { // Only entries NOT managed by PolyLib registration APIs. // Items, blocks, and other objects registered with // PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier) // and accessibility options registered with // AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register(key, builder -> ...) // are included AUTOMATICALLY — no add() calls needed here. add("message.mymod.some_event", "Something happened!"); } } } What is auto-included Any key+English pair contributed to `PolyLangContributions` via:

`AccessibilityOptionsRegistry.register(key, builder → ...)` — all `.toggle()`, `.togglePair()`, and `.category()` labels `ConfigPanelRegistry.register(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, factory, shortcut)` `ConfigPanelRegistry.registerModularGui(modId, labelKey, defaultEnglish, factory, shortcut)` `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry.register(..., displayNameKey, displayNameEnglish)` `PolyRegistry.register(name, defaultEnglish, supplier)` — block/item names `PolyLangContributions.contribute(key, english)` — direct contributions

Locale support Use `String, String)` to generate a locale other than `en_us`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.neoforge.NeoForgeDebugBridge (class, neoforge): NeoForge bridge that wires `PolyDebugRegistry` into the vanilla `DebugScreenEntries` system via `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent`.

Registered on the mod event bus from `net.creeperhost.polylib.PolyLibClientNeoForge`.

Each `PolyDebugEntryType` is adapted to a `DebugScreenEntry` that delegates `isAllowed()` and `display()` back to the `PolyDebugEntry` implementation. Toggle state and persistence are handled entirely by vanilla's `DebugOptions` / `options.txt` mechanism — no extra storage is needed.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.PolyDebugDisplayer (interface, common): Platform-agnostic display interface passed to `PolyDebugEntry#display`.

Maps directly onto `DebugScreenDisplayer` on both NeoForge and Fabric. Use `#addLine` for normal sequential lines, `#addPriorityLine` to force a line to the top of its column, and `#addToGroup` to append lines beneath an existing vanilla or mod-registered entry group.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.PolyDebugEntry (interface, common): Callback interface for a custom F3 debug screen entry.

Implement this interface and register an instance via `PolyDebugRegistry#register`. Both methods are called on the render thread (client-side only), each frame while the F3 screen is visible. Example `PolyDebugRegistry.register( Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "stats"), new PolyDebugEntry() { public boolean isAllowed(Minecraft mc, boolean reduced) { return mc.level != null; // only show in-world ` public void display(PolyDebugDisplayer d, Level level, LevelChunk cc, LevelChunk sc) { d.addLine("MyMod stat: " + MyStats.getValue()); } }, true, true, false, "debug.mymod.stats", "My Stats" ); }
- net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.PolyDebugEntryType (class, common): Typed registration token for a custom F3 debug screen entry.

Obtain via `PolyDebugRegistry#register` and store as a `public static final` constant in your mod class. Toggle / profile behaviour

`#defaultEnabled` — whether the toggle button is ON by default when no saved preference exists yet. MC persists the toggle across sessions in the vanilla `options.txt` (`debugScreen.*`). `#inDefaultProfile` — automatically enable this entry when the player activates the "Default" F3 profile (F3 + N in vanilla). `#inPerformanceProfile` — automatically enable this entry when the "Performance" F3 profile is active.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.PolyDebugRegistry (class, common): Registry for `PolyDebugEntryType` tokens.

Registration must happen before the debug screen is first opened — typically in your mod's client initialiser or static init. On NeoForge this registry is consumed by `net.creeperhost.polylib.debug.neoforge.NeoForgeDebugBridge` during the `RegisterDebugEntriesEvent` (mod bus). On Fabric it is consumed by the `FabricDebugEntriesMixin` injected into `DebugScreenEntries`. Minimal usage example `// In your mod client init: public static final PolyDebugEntryType MY_ENTRY = PolyDebugRegistry.register( Identifier.fromNamespaceAndPath("mymod", "my_info"), displayer -> displayer.addLine("MyMod: " + getSomeValue()), true, // ON by default true, // included in the Default profile false, // not in the Performance profile "debug.mymod.my_info", // i18n key "My Info" // English fallback for datagen ); `
- net.creeperhost.polylib.event.data.CancelContext (class, common): Passed to cancellable PolyEvent handlers. Handlers call `#cancel()` to stop further propagation. The combiner for cancellable events must check `#isCancelled()` after each handler and short-circuit.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.inventory.PlayerInventoryMirrorContainer (class, common): A live Container view of a ServerPlayer's inventory (main + armor + offhand) plus any Curios slots appended by the platform layer. Slot layout (matches VoidAnomalyEntity.SNAPSHOT_SIZE = 41): 0-35 main inventory (including hotbar 0-8) 36-39 armor slots (feet, legs, chest, head) 40 offhand 41+ curios slots (appended by CuriosPlayerInventoryMirror if Curios is present) This container does NOT copy items — every read/write goes directly to the player's live Inventory, so changes are immediately visible to the player without any sync step.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.mixin.client.EntryMapAccessor (interface, fabric): Mixin accessor that exposes the private-static `ENTRIES_BY_ID` field of `DebugScreenEntries` so that `FabricDebugEntriesMixin` can insert PolyLib debug entries after vanilla's static initialiser runs.

Mutable access is intentional: we need to `Map#put` into the live map, not a copy. The field is a `HashMap` (confirmed via bytecode) that is later read (but not replaced) by `allEntries()` and `getEntry()`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.mixin.client.FabricChatComponentMixin (class, fabric): No summary.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.mixin.client.FabricDebugEntriesMixin (class, fabric): Fabric bridge for `PolyDebugRegistry`.

Injects at the tail of `DebugScreenEntries`'s static initialiser so that all entries registered via `PolyDebugRegistry` are appended to the vanilla `ENTRIES_BY_ID` map before the first F3 screen render.

Because `register(Identifier, DebugScreenEntry)` is private-static, we obtain the `ENTRIES_BY_ID` field via the `EntryMapAccessor` interface and call `Map#put` directly. This matches exactly what the private method does (see bytecode: `ENTRIES_BY_ID.put(id, entry); return id;`).

- net.creeperhost.polylib.platform.FabricPlayerDataHelper (class, fabric): Fabric implementation of `IPlayerDataHelper`. The `copyOnDeath()` flag mirrors `PlayerClientSettingsType#copyOnDeath()`.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.platform.NeoForgePlayerDataHelper (class, neoforge): NeoForge implementation of `IPlayerDataHelper`.

Client settings (StreamCodec-based): stored as `byte[]` in `player.getPersistentData()` under key `polylib_settings.`.

Server data (DFU Codec-based): stored as a wrapped NBT tag in `player.getPersistentData()` under key `polylib_sdata.`. The tag is wrapped in a CompoundTag (`{v: `}) to handle all NBT element types.

Both are saved with the player NBT automatically and loaded on join.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.platform.services.IPlayerDataHelper (interface, common): Platform service for persisting player data (both client settings and server data). NeoForge impl uses `getPersistentData()` (CompoundTag) for both. Fabric impl uses `AttachmentRegistry` for both.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.platform.services.IRegisterHelper (interface, common): No summary.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.offline.OfflinePlayerData (interface, common): Mutable view of a single player's PolyLib server data, valid for either an online or offline player. Obtained via `java.util.UUID, java.util.function.Consumer)`.

For online players every `#get`/`#set` call goes directly to `net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataManager`. For offline players the view is backed by the loaded `ForgeData` `net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag`; changes are written back to `/playerdata/.dat` when the `modify` call returns.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.offline.OfflinePlayerDataAccessor (class, common): Read/write PolyLib `PlayerServerDataType` values for both online and offline players. Online players All operations delegate to the live `PlayerServerDataManager` so the in-memory store is never bypassed. Offline players Data is read from / written to the player's `.dat` file at `/playerdata/.dat`. The exact NBT structure used is platform-specific: NeoForge stores data inside the `ForgeData` compound; Fabric uses the `fabric:attachments` compound. Thread safety Must be called from the server tick thread. No locking is performed because Minecraft's server is single-threaded; concurrent calls from other threads (e.g. the network thread) are unsafe regardless. Usage example `// One-shot read (returns default if no data) PlayerAbilities ab = OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.get(server, uuid, ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES); // One-shot write OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.set(server, uuid, ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES, newAbilities); // Atomic read-modify-write (single file I/O pass for offline players) OfflinePlayerDataAccessor.modify(server, uuid, data -> { PlayerAbilities ab = data.get(ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES); ab.addPower(SomePower.ID); data.set(ModPlayerData.PLAYER_ABILITIES, ab); `); }
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataClientCache (class, common): Client-side read-only cache of server-authoritative player data values.

Values are received via `SyncPlayerServerDataS2CPayload` and decoded on demand using the type's `syncCodec`. This cache is keyed by type ID only (not UUID) because these values are always for the local/owning player.

Typical use: HUD rendering, client-side power availability checks. Never write to this; mutations go through `PlayerServerDataManager#set` on the server.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataManager (class, common): Central server-side manager for `PlayerServerDataType` values.

Handles NBT persistence (via `IPlayerDataHelper`), optional S2C sync to the owning player, and player lifecycle (login / logout / respawn).

Server is always the authoritative source. Use `#get` / `#set` from server-side code only. Clients receive a read-only copy via `PlayerServerDataClientCache` when the type's `syncCodec` is non-null.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataRegistry (class, common): Registry for `PlayerServerDataType` tokens. All registration must happen before the server starts (mod constructor / init).
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataStore (class, common): Per-player in-memory store for server-authoritative player data values. Internal to PolyLib — not part of the public API. Mirrors `PlayerClientSettingsStore` but keyed on `PlayerServerDataType`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.PlayerServerDataType (class, common): Typed token representing a registered server-authoritative player data type.

Create via `PlayerServerDataRegistry#register` and store as a `public static final` constant in your mod.

This is the server-authority counterpart to `PlayerClientSettingsType`. The server owns the value; the client receives read-only S2C syncs for HUD use.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.serverdata.SyncPlayerServerDataS2CPayload (record, common): S2C packet: server pushes an updated server-authoritative data value to the owning player. Sent only to the player whose data changed — never to other players.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.BroadcastScope (enum, common): Controls which clients receive S2C sync packets when a PlayerClientSetting value changes.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingsClientCache (class, common): Client-side cache of PlayerClientSettings values received via S2C sync packets. Replaces per-mod caches like `PlayerAppearanceCache`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingsManager (class, common): Central server-side manager for PlayerClientSettings. Handles persistence, sync, and incoming C2S updates.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingsRegistry (class, common): Registry for `PlayerClientSettingsType` tokens. All registration must happen before the server starts (typically in mod constructor or init).
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingsStore (class, common): Per-player in-memory store for PlayerClientSettings values. Internal to PolyLib — not part of public API. Provides zero-deserialization reads via a typed object cache.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingsType (class, common): Typed token representing a registered PlayerClientSetting type. Create via `PlayerClientSettingsRegistry#register` and store as a `public static final` constant in your mod.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.PlayerClientSettingSyncS2CPayload (record, common): S2C: server broadcasts a PlayerClientSetting value update to clients per the type's `BroadcastScope`.
- net.creeperhost.polylib.player.settings.UpdatePlayerClientSettingC2SPayload (record, common): C2S: client sends an updated PlayerClientSetting value to the server.

- net.creeperhost.polylib.registry.PolyScreens (class, common): Cross-platform screen registration queue.

Call `#register` from client-only init code (e.g. inside an `isClient()` guard). Platform entry points flush the queue at the appropriate time:

NeoForge — call `NeoPolyScreens.registerToBus(bus)` from your mod constructor; the flush happens during `RegisterMenuScreensEvent`. Fabric — call `#flush` from your `ClientModInitializer.onInitializeClient()`.
